name: TypingMind
tagline: A polished bring-your-own-API-key chat frontend for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and friends.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Historically sold as a one-time license with paid tiers, plus a hosted/team option.

verdictSummary: The core of TypingMind is a chat window that talks to model APIs with your own key, stores conversations locally, and lets you save prompts and switch models. That is a genuinely easy one-shot: streaming responses, a conversation sidebar, markdown rendering, model picker, all in an afternoon. What you will not one-shot is the long tail: plugins, web search, image and file attachments, vision, voice input, custom agents, cloud sync across devices, and a mobile-usable layout that does not fight you. None of that is protected by anything except the accumulated work of shipping it. So you get 80 percent fast and then discover the last 20 percent is where you actually live.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that streams chat completions from your own provider keys, keeps conversations and saved prompts in browser storage, and lets you switch models mid-thread.
requirements: API keys for at least one model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google)
Somewhere to host it if you want access from your phone
whatYouLose: Plugins and tool use: web search, code execution, image generation wired up and working
File and image attachments with sensible chunking and vision support
Cross-device sync and encrypted cloud backup of your chat history
Voice input, text to speech, and a mobile layout that is actually pleasant
Years of small UX fixes: token counting, branching, prompt library, export formats
moatNotes: No data moat, no network. Just a lot of shipped features around a thin API call, which is the hardest kind of thing to replicate in one sitting.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a one-time license is cheap compared to a weekend of your life, and because the product keeps absorbing new provider APIs, new modalities, and new plugin surfaces without you doing anything. If your usage is a text chat with occasional model switching, the DIY build is legitimately fine and cheaper forever. If you use attachments, search, voice, or want the same history on your laptop and your phone, you will slowly rebuild TypingMind and do it worse.
notes: The chat box is trivial; everything bolted to the chat box is not. Build it if you only ever type words at a model.
prompt:
Build a local-first, single-user AI chat frontend called "MyChat". No accounts, no backend database, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- A tiny Node/Express server in the same repo used ONLY as a proxy for provider API calls so keys never sit in client bundles
- Conversation storage in IndexedDB via the idb package
- pnpm, Node 20+

Features in scope:
1. Left sidebar: list of conversations with title, last-updated time, search box, new chat button, delete and rename.
2. Main pane: message thread with streaming assistant responses (SSE from the proxy), markdown rendering via react-markdown, GitHub-flavored tables, and syntax-highlighted code blocks with a copy button.
3. Model picker in the header. Support OpenAI chat completions and Anthropic messages. Model list is a hardcoded array in src/models.ts with provider, id, display name, and context window. Switching models mid-conversation is allowed and the next request just uses the new one.
4. Per-conversation system prompt, editable in a collapsible panel.
5. A prompt library: named reusable prompts stored in IndexedDB, inserted into the composer with a slash command menu.
6. Settings modal: temperature, max tokens, and which providers are configured (read from the server, never show the raw keys).
7. Stop generation button that aborts the fetch and keeps the partial message.
8. Export a conversation as markdown or JSON.
9. Keyboard shortcuts: cmd+k for conversation search, cmd+enter to send, up-arrow in empty composer to edit last message.

Explicitly out of scope: file uploads, images, vision, voice, web search, plugins, cloud sync, multi-user, sharing links.

Keys: OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY read from .env on the server only. Commit a .env.example. The app must start and show a clear "no provider configured" state if both are missing.

Deliver a README with pnpm install, pnpm dev (runs client and proxy together via concurrently), and pnpm build. Include a couple of vitest tests for the streaming parser and the IndexedDB layer. Keep the whole thing under roughly 1500 lines and do not add a state management library beyond React context.
